title: Your iPhone Duo Under Attack? Binance Flags Dangerous iOS Security Flaw
description: Binance warns iPhone users that an iOS flaw could expose crypto seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials through malicious apps. The post Your iPhone Duo Under Attack? Binance Flags Dangerous iOS Security Flaw appeared first on Cryptonews.
content:
Binance has warned Apple users about a dangerous iOS vulnerability that could expose crypto wallets, private keys, and login credentials. The flaw, called worse_query, allows malicious applications to access files normally isolated inside other apps. Binance warning identifies several affected iOS software versions and urges users to remove untrusted applications immediately.

The vulnerability threatens more than crypto wallets; apps storing sensitive information locally could also expose passwords, authentication data, and personal files. That makes the latest warning particularly concerning for iPhone users who rely on their devices for banking and crypto transactions.

Binance says the problem affects iOS itself rather than its own wallet infrastructure. Users who suspect their devices have been compromised should create new wallets on clean devices and move their funds. The exchange also recommends resetting active login sessions and updating installed software.

Binance Warns A Dangerous iOS Sandbox Escape

The vulnerability exploits Apple’s application sandbox, a security mechanism designed to keep applications separated from one another. Normally, an application cannot freely access another application’s private files. This isolation protects sensitive information even when users install multiple applications on the same device.

This is where it gets dangerous: the worse_query exploit reportedly bypasses those restrictions. A malicious application could potentially access directories containing information belonging to other installed applications.

The researcher behind the public GitHub repository describes worse_query as a sandbox escape affecting iOS 26 and iOS 27. The project identifies affected releases spanning iOS 26.0 through 26.7.2 and iOS 27.2. Binance warns that exposed information could include cryptocurrency recovery phrases, private keys, and login credentials.

The actual danger depends partly on how individual applications store sensitive information. Wallets retaining recovery phrases or other credentials in accessible local files face particular risks.

Security researchers have also highlighted the importance of protecting plaintext wallet information. SlowMist’s security chief warned that the vulnerability could undermine assumptions about isolation between application containers.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Apple Users Face Questions Over Security Updates

Apple’s security update schedule adds another dimension to the Binance iOS warning. Apple’s security releases list iOS 27.2 and iOS 26.7.2 among its available software versions, both released on October 26, 2026.

However, Apple’s published security advisories do not explicitly identify worse_query by name. There is currently no confirmed public statement establishing that these updates fully resolve the specific sandbox escape.

A separate GitHub project implementing the exploit also reported on November 8 that Apple’s available software releases had not patched worse_query. This leaves users with an important gap between installing the latest available update and confirming that a particular vulnerability has been fixed.

Binance recommends installing the latest official iOS release and keeping all applications updated. It also urges users to remove applications from unknown sources, including manually signed IPA files.

For us, crypto holders, the safest response to suspected compromise goes beyond simply deleting suspicious software.

Previous iPhone Attacks Put Crypto Wallets in the Spotlight

The latest iPhone warning follows several security incidents involving malicious applications and crypto credentials. In September, Binance warned users about FomoPeek, a third-party application whose versions 1.1 and 1.2 reportedly contained malicious code.

Security researchers found that the software could exploit iOS vulnerabilities to obtain elevated device privileges. Potentially exposed information included recovery phrases, private keys, login credentials, and other locally stored data.

More recently, CertiK highlighted the DarkSword exploit framework, which reportedly targeted cryptocurrency applications through compromised websites and vulnerable iPhones.

These incidents involve separate attack methods. Nevertheless, they demonstrate why smartphone security has become increasingly important for crypto holders.

The Binance iOS warning highlights a fundamental problem with self-custody: protecting a recovery phrase means protecting every place where that information might be stored.

title: Cardano Concludes Epoch 666 as ADA Tests Critical $0.17 Support
description: Cardano has surpassed 127 million recorded mainnet transactions, although cumulative activity alone cannot establish recent adoption growth. DijkstraNet is testing protocol version 12, while Midnights Ledger 9 upgrade expands compatibility with established cryptographic standards. ADA remains below ...
content:
• Cardano has surpassed 127 million recorded mainnet transactions, although cumulative activity alone cannot establish recent adoption growth.
  • DijkstraNet is testing protocol version 12, while Midnight’s Ledger 9 upgrade expands compatibility with established cryptographic standards.
  • ADA remains below its major moving averages, with a break beneath nearby support potentially exposing deeper losses.

Cardano’s epoch 666, a routine five-day proof-of-stake cycle that attracted attention because of its biblical association, is concluding without a corresponding mainnet upgrade. The network’s more substantive developments involve Dijkstra testing and Midnight’s cryptographic improvements.

Meanwhile, ADA faces a separate challenge. Its daily chart shows a persistent decline from October’s highs, with price approaching an established support zone as momentum remains close to oversold territory.

Cardano’s Development Pipeline Moves Beyond Epoch 666

According to Cexplorer, the network has recorded 127,203,164 mainnet transactions since launch.

The figure provides a cumulative measure of blockchain activity, but not a reliable indication of current demand. Establishing whether usage is accelerating would require comparable daily transaction counts, active-address figures and fee data across consistent periods.

Development activity offers a more immediate view of Cardano’s technical direction.

DijkstraNet has transitioned to protocol version 12, making the Dijkstra feature set available for testing and integration, excluding Linear Leios.

Node 11.2, pre-released on October 28, supported the transition, while DB Sync 13.8.0.0 provides updated infrastructure for applications and services that index blockchain data.

For stake-pool operators and developers, the practical significance is an opportunity to test compatibility before broader deployment. Testnet availability does not establish a mainnet activation date.

Linear Leios remains outside the current DijkstraNet feature set, meaning the transition should not be interpreted as delivery of Cardano’s longer-term scaling roadmap.

Midnight Adds Tools Familiar to Ethereum Developers

Midnight has separately completed its Ledger 8-to-Ledger 9 upgrade, adding native support for ECDSA and Keccak-256.

These capabilities matter because Ethereum-compatible software commonly relies on the same cryptographic primitives.

ECDSA enables verification of signatures produced using supported elliptic-curve schemes, while Keccak-256 supports hashing operations used throughout Ethereum’s application ecosystem.

Their availability could reduce the amount of custom cryptographic implementation required when developers adapt existing tools or verification logic for Midnight.

However, support for these primitives does not automatically establish Ethereum Virtual Machine compatibility, cross-chain asset transfers or interoperability with existing wallets. Those functions require additional protocol and application infrastructure.

The upgrade is therefore best understood as an improvement in developer compatibility rather than evidence of an immediate increase in Cardano mainnet activity.

ADA Price Analysis: Descending Channel Threatens Support

At the time of writing Cardano is trading at $0.17747 following a decline from October’s local highs near $0.28.

The price action has formed a descending parallel channel, marked by successive lower highs and lower lows. The latest candles remain inside that structure, with sellers retaining control of the intermediate trend.

The moving averages reinforce the weakness, although their ordering reveals a lagging transition rather than a completed bearish alignment.

The 50-day SMA stands at $0.22286, above the 100-day average at $0.21330 and the 200-day average at $0.20616. Despite this ordering, ADA trades beneath all three indicators, suggesting the recent selloff has developed faster than the longer-period averages can adjust.

A continuation of the downtrend could eventually produce bearish moving-average crossovers, but those signals have not yet occurred.

Momentum offers little evidence of an established reversal. The 14-day RSI stands at 32.72, marginally below its signal average of 33.09.

The indicator is approaching the conventional oversold threshold of 30. However, oversold conditions can persist during strong downtrends, and the chart does not show a clearly confirmed bullish RSI divergence.

The Price Levels That Matter

The chart identifies four horizontal reference levels associated with previous areas of price reaction. These levels provide a framework for assessing potential recovery attempts and further downside.

A sustained move above the descending channel’s upper boundary would be the first indication that sellers are losing control. Confirmation would require buyers to defend the breakout on a subsequent retest rather than allowing price to fall back inside the channel.

The longer-term moving averages remain an additional obstacle, particularly the 200-day SMA near $0.20616.

On the downside, a daily close beneath the nearest horizontal support would weaken the current trading range and increase the probability of another test of lower demand areas.

The channel’s lower boundary provides a separate, downward-sloping reference. Its exact value changes over time and should not be treated as identical to any fixed horizontal level.

A breakdown accompanied by expanding selling volume would carry greater technical weight than a brief intraday move beneath support.

What Would Change ADA’s Bearish Outlook?

The current chart presents two different confirmation tests.

For buyers, the priority is to interrupt the sequence of lower highs and establish a higher low outside the descending channel. An RSI recovery above 50 would strengthen the momentum picture, although it is not necessary for an initial rebound.

For sellers, a decisive loss of support would reinforce the existing trend, particularly if followed by a failed attempt to reclaim the broken level.

Neither outcome can be assigned a reliable probability from the available chart alone. The screenshot does not provide sufficient volume or derivatives-positioning data to establish whether the decline is approaching exhaustion.

Cardano’s development releases offer separate milestones, but they do not establish a direct catalyst for ADA’s price recovery.

For traders, the immediate evidence remains in the market structure: a confirmed breakout would require sustained buying above resistance, while failure to defend support would leave the descending trend intact.

title: Bybit Says $17.3B Proof of Reserves Covers 50 Assets, but the Audit Has Limits
description: Bybit says the latest snapshot of its proof-of-reserves system covered $17.3 billion in customer assets across 50 cryptocurrencies. The exchange's November 3 announcement describes its 41st report, with figures independently checked by security…
content:
TL;DR: Bybit says the latest snapshot of its proof-of-reserves system covered $17.3 billion in customer assets across 50 cryptocurrencies. The exchange's November 3 announcement describes its 41st report, with figures independently checked by security firm Hacken against an October 27 snapshot.

Bybit says the latest snapshot of its proof-of-reserves system covered $17.3 billion in customer assets across 50 cryptocurrencies. The exchange's November 3 announcement describes its 41st report, with figures independently checked by security firm Hacken against an October 27 snapshot. The exercise offers a view of assets and customer balances at a specific moment, but it should not be mistaken for an all-purpose guarantee that an exchange could meet every liability under every scenario.

The ratios behind the headline

Bybit says its reserve ratios exceeded 100% across all 50 covered assets, including 112% for USDT, 405% for USDC, 102% for Bitcoin and 101% for Ether. Those percentages compare identified reserves with customer balances under the stated methodology. An unusually high ratio for one token does not mean the business has the same excess in every asset or that reserves could be freely moved between customer pools. Readers should also distinguish a token-by-token reserve ratio from consolidated corporate solvency, which incorporates obligations that may not appear in a proof-of-reserves snapshot.

Why the snapshot date matters

The release identifies the audit point as October 27 at 06:00 UTC. Reserve balances, withdrawals, borrowing, market prices and off-exchange exposures may have changed after that time. The value of recurring disclosures lies partly in their comparability: users can look for persistent gaps or unexpected movements rather than treating a single publication as permanent reassurance. Bybit says the checks covered the 50 listed crypto assets, but the exact perimeter, included customer categories and handling of institutional arrangements are questions worth reviewing in the detailed report.

What an independent check can and cannot establish

The exchange says Hacken carried out the verification. Third-party involvement is useful, particularly when the reviewer explains its methods and limitations, but the word 'audit' can be interpreted too broadly. A Merkle-tree exercise may allow customers to verify that a balance was included while proving possession of identified onchain assets. It does not, by itself, necessarily establish that there are no undisclosed debts, encumbrances, affiliated-party claims or operational weaknesses. The scope of work therefore deserves as much attention as the name of the verifier.

Customer protection still has other layers

Asset backing is a fundamental question for custodial exchanges because users depend on the firm to return assets they cannot directly control. Yet security controls, market surveillance, legal ownership of customer property, segregation practices and withdrawal resilience also matter. A fully funded snapshot is only one component of a broader risk picture. The report can be especially informative when combined with clear explanations of liabilities, independent financial statements where available and timely incident reporting. It should not substitute for personal decisions about custodial concentration.

How readers should use the results

Bybit users can inspect the methodology and verify balances if the relevant tool supports that check. External analysts should compare successive reports and look for consistency between claimed assets and observable onchain holdings. Markets benefit from more systematic disclosures, but transparent limitations are an important part of credible transparency. The milestone is the reporting process, not a declaration that counterparty risk has disappeared.

Primary source: Bybit proof-of-reserves announcement. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s analysis of earnings and stablecoin activity at another major exchange.

Speaking in the White House, the president said the US remained ‘locked and loaded’ but escalation was not needed. Plus, how Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Oil prices have dropped after Donald Trump unilaterally declared that the US war on Iran was “effectively over”. During a White House press conference, Trump said Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.

He said, however, that the US remained “locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason”, adding: “We’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.” Brent crude has dropped below $90, its lowest level since August.

What is the latest development with Pete Hegseth? A Republican lawmaker has moved to force a vote to impeach the US defense secretary. Thomas Massie, of Kentucky, introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, accusing him of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers.

What has happened at a US airbase in England? The US military has reportedly evacuated aircraft from a second airbase in ⁠Britain after a threat from Iran. Two US refuelling tankers that were using the RAF Mildenhall military base diverted to Germany on Monday morning, while several other tankers at the base ⁠were moved to Germany and other locations later in the day.
